description.narrative:
In August 2021, the Ministry of Education, the Federation of Kenya Employers (FKE) and the Central Organization of Trade Unions (COTU), the National Qualification Authority, revised and validated the Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework and Implementation guideline. The framework enhances the inclusion of refugees, youth and other vulnerable and marginalized target groups with skills acquired outside of the formal system. The new policy framework outlines the process of identifying, documenting and assessing informal learning against formal training education and training standards. It focuses on the outcome of knowledge and learning that is acquired through work experience.
Assessment tools for Welding, Automotive, Textile, Hair and Beauty Therapy sub sectors in Kenya were developed. As a pilot, 36 youth assessed have undergone the RPL process using the reviewed RPL framework. With the support of FCDO and the Government of the Netherlands, the ILO advised and facilitated the establishment and operationalization of a tripartite national steering committee on RPL. The ILO further built the capacity of the Steering committee members through training and coaching on designing the national RPL framework and its implementation tools. In addition, the ILO facilitated the piloting of the RPL assessment mechanism. The ILO also reviewed the RPL framework and implementation tools to ensure alignment with ILO recommendations and guiding tools.

Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: In May 2020, the County Governments of Nakuru, Narok, Turkana, Garissa, and the Federation of Kenya Employers, operationalized procurement opportunities support programmes for locals SMEs in four value chains; leather production, beadwork, hotel industry and solar energy, to access markets in large companies in the Counties. The intervention targeted youth and women owned enterprises. With the support of Government of Netherlands and Sweden, in the period between January and March 2020, ILO facilitated building capacities and certification of 50 Business Development Service Providers in Nakuru, Narok, Turkana, Garissa and Turkan counties using the ILO Start and Improve Your Business Management Tool. These training aimed at Micro Small and Medium size enterprises and cover core business management skills that are required to start and run sustainable enterprises such as business plan development, record keeping, costing, marketing, financial planning and human resources management. The trained trainers later on conducted training of 661 new and existing youth and women owned enterprises to enhance their business skills, access to entrepreneurship training, digital marketing, business support services. this further facilitated registration support to 300 SMEs with the local chamber of Commerce for direct market linkages with large companies.

Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
In May 2021, the Busia County Government developed an "Apprenticeship Training Policy" in collaboration with the Federation of Kenya Employers (FKE), Central Organization of Trade Unions (COTU), Department of Labour, Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA), and National Industrial Training Authority (NITA). The policy supports quality workplace-based training opportunities, including apprenticeships and internships for youth, targeting vulnerable and marginalized people in rural areas. A tripartite validation process enhanced the role of the Workplace-Based Training Coordination Committees (WBTCC) as platforms for coordination, resource mobilization, and social dialogue on skills development.
Increased access to workplace-based learning for 227 vulnerable youth and women in 7 Counties (Kilifi, Busia, Kitui, Turkana, Narok, Nakuru, Garissa) was facilitated through: - Development and review of 7 National Occupational Standards by National Curriculum Development institutions, social partners and the private sector. . Development of pedagogy skills upgrading curriculum for Master Crafts Persons to enhance quality Workplace Based Training for youth, with enterprises. - Development of manuals for pre-apprenticeship training for Apprenticeship providers, in partnership with TVETA. - Review of National Occupational Safety and Health manuals and protocols targeting micro and Small Enterprises. - Development of 20 public-private partnerships to provide youth and women with workplace-based training on technical and soft skills.
Since January 2020, the County Governments of Narok and Nakuru, in partnership with the FKE and the Kenya Electricity Generating Company Ltd (KenGen PLC), implemented an up-skilling programme for industry instructors/in–company trainers, benefiting 600 youth and women. A Memorandum of Understanding was signed between KenGen PLC and vocational training Centres. With support of the Government of Sweden (SIDA) and in partnership with the Ministry of Education and TVET CDACC, the County Governments of Nakuru and Narok, and private sector organizations, the ILO supported the review of National Occupational Standards and Competency Based Curricula in five demand driven trade areas and the development of training materials (February 2021). In addition, since January 2020, the ILO facilitated consultations and social dialogue to encourage linkages between learning institutions, private and public partners in order to promote quality industry driven skills. With support of United States Department of Labor (USDOL), the ILO did an assessment of gaps in existing policies and laws, governing apprenticeship training with focus on inclusion of youth, including vulnerable and marginalized young men and women (February 2020). Following the recommendations of this assessment, the ILO facilitated consultations with social partners and provided guidance during the development of county Apprenticeship policy, guided by the ILO Toolkit for Quality Apprenticeships - Vol. 1: Guide for Policy Makers. The ILO also supported national and district institutions, as well as social partners, in the establishment of institutional mechanisms (committees) for WBT programmes at national and county level.
